title: A VLT Auxiliary Telescopes watches the Milky Way setting
caption: An Auxiliary Telescope and the setting Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Seen from the platform of ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT) on Paranal, a magnificent Milky Way sets very low over the horizon, with one of the observatory's Auxiliary Telescopes in the foreground. The galaxy's core shows as a yellowish bulge scored with dark dust lanes, and the brightest dot above it is Jupiter.

Catching the Milky Way this low is possible thanks to the exceptional quality of Paranal's sky. Near the horizon, starlight passes through much more air, so only a very clear, dark sky shows the band so well.

The VLT has four 8.2-meter Unit Telescopes and four 1.8-meter Auxiliary Telescopes. The Auxiliary Telescopes are dedicated to interferometry, a technique that lets astronomers see details up to 25 times finer than the individual telescopes can. Running on rails, they can be moved across the platform to 30 different positions.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by G. Hüdepohl. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the low Milky Way may look brighter here than it would to an observer on the platform.
